originalText:
📚 Chart Basics: Support & Resistance
Support = a floor where buyers have shown up before.
Resistance = a ceiling where sellers have shown up before.
✅ Bullish — Support holds: buyers keep defending the level.
🛑 Bearish — Resistance rejects: sellers keep defending the level.
⚖️ Neutral — Stuck in the range: wait for a decisive break of either level.
Which do you mark first on a fresh chart — support or resistance? 👇
#TechnicalAnalysis #Trading

chart.altText: Chart Basics: Support & Resistance. Price levels where buyers or sellers have repeatedly stepped in. Support holds (Bullish): Price dips to the floor and bounces — again. Buyers keep defending the level. Resistance rejects (Bearish): Price rallies to the ceiling and gets sold — again. Sellers keep defending the level. Stuck in the range (Neutral): Price ping-pongs between the two levels. Wait for a decisive break of either level. Educational only. Not financial advice.

setup.setup: AI Trade School Lesson #03: RSI (Relative Strength Index)

originalText:
🎓 AI Trade School — Lesson #03
RSI (Relative Strength Index)
A 0–100 momentum gauge. Above 70 is stretched, below 30 is washed out.
RSI measures how fast price has been moving, not where it is going.
50 is the midline: above it momentum favours buyers, below it sellers.
✅ Bullish — Rising through 50: momentum is with the buyers and not yet stretched.
🛑 Bearish — Falling under 50: momentum is with the sellers.
⚖️ Neutral — Flat around 50: no momentum edge either way.
👇 Do you treat RSI 70 as a warning or as strength?
#TechnicalAnalysis #TradingEducation

chart.altText: AI Trade School Lesson #03: RSI (Relative Strength Index). A 0–100 momentum gauge. Above 70 is stretched, below 30 is washed out. Rising through 50 (Bullish): RSI climbs from the 40s into the 60s and holds. Momentum is with the buyers and not yet stretched. Falling under 50 (Bearish): RSI drops through the midline and keeps sliding. Momentum is with the sellers. Flat around 50 (Neutral): RSI drifts sideways between 45 and 55. No momentum edge either way. Educational only. Not financial advice.

setup.setup: AI Trade School Lesson #04: CMF (Chaikin Money Flow)

originalText:
🎓 AI Trade School — Lesson #04
CMF (Chaikin Money Flow)
Measures whether volume is flowing into or out of an asset over the last 20 bars.
Above zero: closes are landing near the highs on volume — accumulation.
Below zero: closes near the lows on volume — distribution.
✅ Bullish — Positive and rising: money is flowing in while price rises.
🛑 Bearish — Negative and falling: money is leaving even on up days.
⚖️ Neutral — Hugging zero: no conviction from volume yet.
👇 Do you look at price first, or the flow behind it?
#TechnicalAnalysis #TradingEducation

chart.altText: AI Trade School Lesson #04: CMF (Chaikin Money Flow). Measures whether volume is flowing into or out of an asset over the last 20 bars. Positive and rising (Bullish): CMF holds above zero and climbs. Money is flowing in while price rises. Negative and falling (Bearish): CMF stays below zero and sinks. Money is leaving even on up days. Hugging zero (Neutral): CMF wobbles just above and below the line. No conviction from volume yet. Educational only. Not financial advice.

🎓 AI Trade School — Lesson #05
Breakouts
Price closes beyond a level that held before — and stays there.
The close matters more than the poke: a wick through a level is not a breakout.
The old ceiling often becomes the new floor.
✅ Bullish — Clean breakout: confirmed by the close and the retest.
🛑 Bearish — Clean breakdown: the old floor becomes the ceiling.
⚖️ Neutral — Poke, no close: not confirmed. Wait for a close beyond the level.
👇 Do you enter on the break or wait for the retest?
#TechnicalAnalysis #TradingEducation

chart.altText: AI Trade School Lesson #05: Breakouts. Price closes beyond a level that held before — and stays there. Clean breakout (Bullish): A full candle closes above resistance, then holds. Confirmed by the close and the retest. Clean breakdown (Bearish): A full candle closes below support, then fails to reclaim it. The old floor becomes the ceiling. Poke, no close (Neutral): Price trades above the level intraday but closes back under it. Not confirmed. Wait for a close beyond the level. Educational only. Not financial advice.

setup.setup: AI Trade School Lesson #06: Fakeouts (Bull & Bear Traps)

originalText:
🎓 AI Trade School — Lesson #06
Fakeouts (Bull & Bear Traps)
A break that fails fast — price snaps back through the level.
Bull trap: breaks above resistance, then closes back below it.
Bear trap: breaks below support, then reclaims it.
✅ Bullish — Bear trap: sellers got trapped; the snap-back is the signal.
🛑 Bearish — Bull trap: buyers got trapped; the failure is the signal.
⚖️ Neutral — Unresolved: neither side has won yet — give it a close.
👇 Ever been caught in a trap? What tipped you off?
#TechnicalAnalysis #TradingEducation

chart.altText: AI Trade School Lesson #06: Fakeouts (Bull & Bear Traps). A break that fails fast — price snaps back through the level. Bear trap (Bullish): Price dips under support, then closes back above it. Sellers got trapped; the snap-back is the signal. Bull trap (Bearish): Price pops above resistance, then closes back below it. Buyers got trapped; the failure is the signal. Unresolved (Neutral): Price sits right on the level after the break. Neither side has won yet — give it a close. Educational only. Not financial advice.

A wick through a level is not a breakout.
What it means: a close beyond a level that held before — and price staying there.
How traders use it: the close, not the poke, is the signal; a close back under the level negates it.
Enter on the break, or wait for the retest? 👇
